question: What memory isolation contract should OpenClaw ship for `memory-core`: default-on per-user isolation with the new `memory.isolation` config surface, a narrower enabled-only repair, or a larger redesign under the canonical multi-user memory tracker?
rationale: The PR defines a security-sensitive memory boundary plus new config/default behavior, and the correct identity source, accepted options, fail-closed behavior, and legacy memory policy require maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Pause for contract and proof
options.body: Require the branch to align default behavior/options with an approved memory isolation contract and provide redacted two-user builtin/QMD proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the config surface
options.body: Remove unimplemented `scope` and `pathEncoding` options and keep only behavior that is fully wired, tested, and documented.

options.title: Close into canonical tracker
options.body: If maintainers prefer a broader gateway-owned partition design, close this branch after preserving useful analysis on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Pause for contract and proof
recommendation.body: Require the branch to align default behavior/options with an approved memory isolation contract and provide redacted two-user builtin/QMD proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans memory host policy, config/default compatibility, and security-sensitive product behavior where recent history shows strong area involvement.
